report.summary: Chunk 5 of 6 of drift.py: defines check() function with snapshot validation and drift detection logic.
risks: check function | high | Snapshot digest mismatch triggers INVALID_SNAPSHOT but does not block further comparison; items list may contain contradictory findings | Check if function returns early on digest mismatch

handoff.purpose: Define the check() function that compares generated state against a committed snapshot, validating integrity and detecting drift.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Main drift detection function; loads snapshot, validates integrity, compares state, returns DriftReport.

claims.text: A missing snapshot FAILS unless ``write_missing`` is set, which is the explicit 'record a baseline' action rather than the default.
claims.why: Lines 1145-1150: if snapshot is None and not write_missing, returns DriftReport(ok=False, first_run=True) without writing; if write_missing is set, writes snapshot and returns ok=True.

claims.text: The previous default -- write it and report OK -- meant ``rm docs/architecture-state.json`` was a green run, and a green run against nothing is exactly what this file exists to make impossible.
claims.why: The code explicitly checks for missing snapshot and only writes when write_missing is True, thus preventing accidental green runs.

claims.text: A count matching its own list proves only internal arithmetic. These check the lists against reality and against each other, so an entry cannot be pre-seeded to suppress a finding that has not landed yet.
claims.why: Lines 1196-1225 validate that lists contain only existing modules (phantom checks) and that test_only modules are a subset of unreached lists.

claims.text: An accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline (:func:`write_snapshot`), so the baseline alone would read it as 'reached' and call it BECAME ISLAND the moment the module also appears in ``modules``. The acceptance is itself a record that it is an island, so it counts toward what the snapshot knows -- without suppressing anything.
claims.why: The claim about write_snapshot behavior is not verifiable in this chunk; the code here computes baselined_islands = old_islands & old_modules, but does not show how acceptances are handled in writing.

claims.text: What the BASELINE actually establishes. Intersecting with ``modules`` is the teeth behind the subset rule above: an island entry the snapshot's own module list does not back is a hand-edit, and a hand-edit must not be able to suppress the finding it was written to hide.
claims.why: Lines 1236: baselined_islands = old_islands & old_modules ensures only modules that appear in both lists are considered baselined; phantom checks earlier catch entries not in modules.

claims.text: BECAME ISLAND means 'it was REACHED and is not any more'. A module the snapshot recorded as unknown or as an unreached shim was never reached, so it must not be described that way when it degrades into an island.
claims.why: Lines 1241-1243 compute known_unreached = ((old_islands | old_unknown | old_shims) & old_modules) | {accepted keys}, and line 1252 checks was_reached = mod in old_modules and mod not in known_unreached, ensuring only previously reached modules get BECAME_ISLAND.

claims.text: The one thing that can still have moved is its cover: it had a test in the snapshot and does not now.
claims.why: Lines 1249-1251: if mod in baselined_islands and not tested and mod in old_test_only, adds item with kind NEW_ISLAND and detail about losing test cover.

claims.text: Same shape as islands, deliberately not merged into them: the finding a reader gets has to say WHICH kind of unreached this is, because the three remedies are three different sentences.
claims.why: Lines 1272-1290 handle unknown and shims separately with distinct kinds NEW_UNKNOWN and NEW_SHIM, each with their own detail messages.

claims.text: What they share is the property that used to be missing entirely -- a module nothing reaches is COUNTED, is named, and blocks until somebody explains it.
claims.why: The code generates DriftItem entries for every module in state[list_key] that is not baselined or test-only, ensuring each unreached module is reported.

claims.text: It is reported, never merged: merging it is how a dead-branch import used to make its target 'reachable'
claims.why: Lines 1297-1300: for edges in new_index_extra - old_index_extra, adds ENGINE_DISAGREEMENT item; they are not merged into the state.

claims.text: ``new_unreached``, not ``new_islands``: a module that moved from island to shim (or to unknown) is still reached by nothing, and announcing 'something reaches it now' would be the same false-green in a new costume.
claims.why: Lines 1305-1309: for each prefix and old_set, checks if mod not in new_unreached before adding NOW_REACHED, ensuring only modules that left all unreached categories are reported as reached.

observations.what: Digest mismatch does not cause early return; further comparisons proceed with potentially invalid data.
Phantom island check uses old_islands - old_modules, but old_islands may contain entries not in old_modules due to accepted islands; accepted islands are handled separately.
